requested.title: Caller-supplied message keys and attachment descriptors are forwarded verbatim into nodemailer sendMail (local file read / SSRF / raw MIME)
SMTP transport cannot require TLS: opportunistic STARTTLS on the default port 587 leaks AUTH credentials and message bodies to a downgrade attacker
buildTransport silently returns undefined for an unrecognized transport type instead of failing fast at boot
Collected stylesheet is interpolated into <style> without neutralizing a `</style` sequence

parsedVerdicts.reasoning: I verified every code-level claim. `sendEmail()` at mailer.ts:101 destructures only `component`/`props` out and spreads the rest (`...passthrough`) into `resolved` (L102-110), and `SmtpTransport.deliver` at transports.ts:129 does `transporter.sendMail({ ...message })` with no filtering, so any key the caller put on the message object lands in nodemailer. I confirmed the sinks in the installed nodemailer 10.5.0: `dist/esm/mail-composer/index.js` L69-75 replaces the whole MIME tree from `this.mail.raw`; L164-166 promotes `attachment.path` to `href` when it matches `^https?://`; L174-181 streams `{path}` from the local filesystem or fetches `{href}`; and `disableFileAccess`/`disableUrlAccess` are read off `this.mail.*` only, i.e. they default to falsy, so file and URL access are both live. The runtime contract is therefore strictly wider than the declared types: `MochiEmailAttachment` makes `content` required, yet `recordDevEmail`'s `attachmentSize` (devOutbox.ts:49-51) throws a TypeError on a `{path}`-only entry — proving the runtime accepts what the type forbids, and confirming the finding's dev-vs-prod divergence (dev crashes loudly, SMTP silently reads the file). I could not name any runtime mitigation: TypeScript excess-property checking is the only barrier, it does not apply to a spread or to `JSON.parse(body) as MochiEmailMessage`, and mochi publishes raw TS so a JS consumer gets nothing. I checked every in-repo caller (`support/src/jobs.server.ts:32`, `support/src/newsletter/jobs.server.ts:50`, `site/src/demos/email/routes.ts:15,27`, the tests) and all build literal messages from server-controlled data, so there is no reachable path in this repository — this is a latent framework sink that needs a consumer-side mass-assignment bug to fire, which is why MEDIUM (not higher) is the right severity and I am leaving it unchanged. One nuance against the finding's framing: the L98-100 comment explicitly says author-supplied fields 'pass through untouched', so the 'callers assume it is sanitized' argument is weaker than claimed, but the stale transports.ts:126-128 comment ('map 1:1 onto nodemailer's sendMail options') genuinely asserts an invariant the rest-spread does not enforce. The recommendation is correct and cheap: allowlist the transport-bound keys and normalize each attachment to `{filename, content, contentType}`, rejecting `path`/`href`/`raw`.

This one checks out in full and is the most solidly verified of the four. `buildTransporter` (transports.ts:103) destructures exactly `{ host, port, secure, auth, pool, tls }` and forwards only those to `createTransport` (L105-112); `MochiSmtpConfig` (types.ts:58-69) declares the same six fields; and `grep -rn 'requireTLS|ignoreTLS|opportunisticTLS' packages/` returns nothing anywhere in the repo, so there is provably no route for nodemailer's `requireTLS` into the connection — a dynamically assembled config carrying it (the shape `packages/support/src/index.ts:22-29` uses) has it dropped by the destructure at runtime even if a cast got it past tsc. I confirmed the consequence in the installed nodemailer: `dist/esm/smtp-connection/index.js:1500` only issues STARTTLS when `!this.secure && !ignoreTLS && (/[ -]STARTTLS\b/im.test(str) || this.options.requireTLS)`; with STARTTLS absent from the EHLO response and `requireTLS` unset it falls straight through to `_parseEhloExtensions` and emits `connect`, after which AUTH and the message body go over the wire in cleartext. `tls` is not a substitute — nodemailer reads `options.requireTLS` at the connection level and hands `options.tls` to the TLS socket. The default path is the vulnerable one: `resolvedSecure = secure ?? port === 465` and `port ?? 587` (L104/L107), so an unspecified config is plain SMTP on the submission port with opportunistic STARTTLS. This is not theoretical for the repo: `packages/support/.env.example` ships `SMTP_PORT=587` with `SMTP_USER`/`SMTP_PASSWORD` and only a commented-out `SMTP_SECURE=false`, and `packages/docs/116-email.md` shows `port: 587, auth: { user, pass }` in all three of its SMTP examples (lines 25, 105-109, 159, 282) with no TLS-hardening guidance at all. The attack is the textbook STARTTLS-stripping MITM: an active on-path attacker or hostile relay deletes the `250-STARTTLS` capability line and harvests the SMTP account credentials plus every support submission and newsletter confirmation link. A workaround exists (port 465 + `secure: true`, or dropping to a `custom` transport), but the framework's shipped default for a credentialed submission-port transport is downgradable and an app has no knob to harden it — a genuine missing-security-control finding (CWE-319/CWE-757). MEDIUM is appropriate given the active-network-position requirement.

The code facts are exactly as described. The switch at transports.ts:14-23 covers `log`/`dev`/`custom`/`smtp` with no `default:`, so an unrecognized `config.type` falls off the end and the function returns `undefined` despite its declared `EmailTransport` return type (TS permits this only because it proves the union exhaustive). `new CustomTransport(config.send)` is likewise unchecked, so a `custom` entry without `send` yields `this.sendFn === undefined`. I confirmed nothing validates this at boot: `resolveEmailOptions` (config.ts:10-14) copies `o.transport` straight through, `getEmailRuntime` casts `options.email` from `unknown`, and `Mochi.ts:616` only reads `.transport.type` for the viewer gate — it never checks it against the known set, unlike the explicit fail-fast throws right beside it for `cron` names, `cronStorage` and `staticDirs` (Mochi.ts:459-473). The failure mode is as stated: `runtime.transport ??= buildTransport(...)` (mailer.ts:127) assigns `undefined`, `??=` therefore never caches it, and `transport.send(filtered)` at L129 throws an opaque `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'send')` on every send — and in `packages/support` that happens inside a durable queue job that burns all three attempts and marks the submission `failed` (jobs.server.ts:40-50). The honest caveat, which I weighed carefully: TypeScript's discriminated-union exhaustiveness makes both sub-cases unreachable for a consumer writing a literal config, so this needs a cast, an `any`-typed config object, or a plain-JS consumer (mochi publishes raw TS, so JS projects get no enforcement at all). That compile-time barrier is why I am keeping this at BUG rather than treating it as a security issue — it is a real missing fail-fast guard that is inconsistent with the repo's own stated convention, not a defect reachable in idiomatic TS usage. The recommended fix (a `default:` throw naming the accepted types, plus a `typeof config.send === 'function'` assertion, ideally hoisted into `resolveEmailOptions`) is correct.

Verified at the source level. render.ts:39 concatenates the collected stylesheet directly into a head `<style>` with no neutralization, and I confirmed `css` can come from plain `.css` files rather than only Svelte style blocks: `ComponentRegistry.renderStatic` pushes `cssFileUrls` entries *and* `entryImportedCss` → `importedCssUrls` entries into `cssUrls` (ComponentRegistry.ts:1615-1631), and `email/render.test.ts:115-121` already exercises exactly that with an `import './fonts.css'`. I also checked that nothing downstream sanitizes: `stripFontFaces` (cssFontAssets.ts:261-271) uses MagicString surgery so the surrounding CSS text is byte-preserved, and `inline(doc, { keepStyleTags: true })` only parses and re-serializes. The finding's described consequence is correct per the HTML spec: `</style` terminates the RAWTEXT element, so css-inline receives a truncated rule set (the mail ships largely uninlined), and the leftover stylesheet text, being non-whitespace character data in `in head`, forces head→after head→in body and is serialized as visible text at the top of the message body. The repo's own analogous `<script>` path does neutralize (`islandPropsRegistry.ts:68` does `json.replace(/</g, '\u003C')`), and I confirmed via grep that email render is the *only* place in `packages/mochi/src` where non-constant CSS is inlined into a `<style>` element — page routes serve CSS via separate `clientFiles` URLs — so this is a genuine one-off gap, not a repo-wide pattern. The one residual uncertainty, which I am not able to settle by static analysis alone, is whether Bun's CSS printer preserves `</style>` inside a string literal, since imported CSS is bundled with `minify: true` (ComponentRegistry.ts:2196-2203); minification strips the comment variant outright, but a `content: "</style>"` string should survive because CSS string serializers escape only quotes, backslashes and control characters, not `<` or `/`. I agree with the finding's own classification that this is not a security issue — `css` is compiler output from developer-authored or third-party sources, never request data — so BUG is correct, and the suggested `replaceAll('</style', '<\\/style')` or passing the sheet to css-inline out-of-band via `extraCss` is the right fix.
